quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It makes you feel overly confident.
It impairs your ability to think clearly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. Your vision and ability to judge distance also get worse after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow at a traffic light, you should:

options.text: Wait until the light turns green.
Stop, then turn in the direction shown by the arrow.
Turn in the direction shown by the arrow when it is safe.
Speed up and turn quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction shown by the arrow when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction if the intersection is clear. You have the right-of-way, but stay alert for other drivers and pedestrians who may be in the intersection illegally.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic at a school, you must:

options.text: Follow the crossing guard's directions.
Follow what other cars are doing instead of the guard's directions.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow normal traffic rules as if children were not present.

questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and use extra caution in school zones, whether a guard is present or not.

questions.question: You can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving by:

options.text: Leaving extra time for your trip.
Following posted speed limits.
Using your turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use your turn signals, follow speed limits, and give yourself plenty of time to reach your destination.

questions.question: Highway hypnosis can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep before your trip.
Driving short distances on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for a long time without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead and stop scanning the road around you. This can cause you to zone out and miss traffic slowing or stopping in front of you.

questions.question: Highway markings:

options.text: Are usually not important.
Are only found in construction zones.
Give drivers important information.
Are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help you position your vehicle correctly, show safe passing zones, and warn you about upcoming hazards.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must drive slowly and honk your horn.
A bus stop is nearby.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you to slow down and watch for children. A school zone is ahead.

questions.question: Driving at night is harder than driving during the day because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
You cannot see as well in the dark.
It rains more at night.
You are more likely to see motorcycles at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as well in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, your vision is limited. Always use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: To drive safely at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
Not drive if you feel tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, visibility is reduced. Follow these steps to make night driving safer for yourself and other drivers.

questions.question: To avoid hitting the car in front of you, you should:

options.text: Watch for hazards ahead.
Watch for brake lights ahead.
Use the four-second rule.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Watch for brake lights and hazards ahead. Keep a four-second distance between your car and the car in front of you when driving under good conditions.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should make sure your physical condition is good. What should you do?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Only drive within your physical limits.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition is important for safe driving. You should know your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you don't see other cars.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you don't see other cars.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you change lanes, turn, or pull away from a curb. Do not skip this step and form bad driving habits.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area. This tells other drivers what you plan to do and helps prevent accidents.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Look both ways at the intersection.
Always come to a full stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Drink coffee.
Open your window.
Stop driving.
Turn on the radio.

questions.explanation: Driving when tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence. If you feel tired, stop driving.

questions.question: Traffic signs and pavement markings:

options.text: Must always be obeyed.
Are just suggestions.
Must be followed only when other cars are present.
Must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and tell drivers about road conditions. You must always obey them.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:

options.text: Make turning harder.
Are more likely to hydroplane.
Can make it take longer to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires can increase your stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without enough tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Signal your lane change.
Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When changing lanes, always signal first, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Changing lanes.
Pulling into or out of a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when leaving a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, you should:

options.text: Get out of their way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing.
Block the passing lane.

questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact with an angry driver. Speeding up can make them angrier and more dangerous.
